issues: At the end of the circle wipe (t=17.7-18.6, d=1.0) the .ax-dark clip-path circle(140% at 50% 115%) does not cover the top of the tall mobile viewport: a ~50-60px ivory arc remains across the top edge, producing a visible ivory seam over the dark transit scene during the pin handoff. Math: percentage radius resolves against sqrt(390^2+844^2)/sqrt(2)=657.6px, so 140% = 921px, while the distance from the center (195, 970) to the top corners is 990px. Raising the final radius to ~165-175% (or using circle(140% at 50% 105%)) closes it. Desktop 1920x800 needs only ~91% so it is unaffected.

action_items: MOBILE ONLY: increase the archive exit-wipe final radius (currently circle(140% at 50% 115%) in the mobile matchMedia block of ArchiveScene.jsx) to ~170% so the top corners are covered at 9:19.5 aspect — currently a ~50-60px ivory band is visible at d=1.0.
critical_code_review_comments: Timeline totals are asserted only implicitly by tween end times; the rail-duration trap (30.7 vs 28.8) recurred because the drift tween duration is a hand-copied literal. Derive it from a single TOTAL constant (e.g. const D_TOTAL = 28.8 / M_TOTAL = 18.6) and use it for both the rail duration and the wipe start so the two can never drift apart again.

The exit-wipe radius is a hard-coded 140% shared conceptually between desktop and mobile; it is aspect-ratio dependent and silently under-covers tall viewports. Compute or over-specify it (>=170%) rather than tuning per breakpoint by eye.
ArchiveScene.jsx (435 lines) is fine on size, but the empty comment block at line 421 ('final resolved statement') is now dead after the resolve removal — remove it to avoid confusion.

rca_of_the_issue: Mobile ivory seam: CSS circle() percentage radii resolve against sqrt(w^2+h^2)/sqrt(2), so on a 390x844 viewport 140% = 921px while the farthest corner from the wipe origin (50% 115%) is 990px away, leaving the top ~50-60px band unfilled at the end of the tween. Not a timeline/scrub bug — purely an insufficient radius constant.
